messages.author: 94ee896ae0b97baf
messages.subject: CFA- two indicators
parts:
Hello everyone,

Hope you are doing well. This question came to my mind this morning. A latent variable needs to have at least three indicators. But two of my latent variables( emotional health, physical health) have TWO indicators... do I need to do anything below my code ? Your insight would be greatly appreciated...

model<-

‘Stress= ~ a+b+c

Emotional health = ~ d+e

Physical health= ~f +g ‘

fit.<-cfa(model, data=spring, missing=”FIML” )

summary (fit, fit.measures=TRUE)

messages.author: 73fb61795976b321
messages.subject: Re: CFA- two indicators
parts:
Hi Su,

Your model is underidentified. Make the loadings of  d and e the same. Do the same, for loadings of f and g.

Regards,

Hugo

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: CFA- two indicators
parts: What if they are not on the same matric? It looks like they are not on the same metric.

I don't think that is really necessary.  If you fix both loadings to 1 and estimate the factor variance, the estimated factor variance should match the observed covariance between those 2 indicators (i.e., the common variance is the common variance).  The idea that fixing a loading to 1 passes the indicator's metric to the factor is a very common misunderstanding with a lot of inertia:  https://psycnet.apa.org/doi/10.1037/1082-989X.7.2.210

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
